note: Rabbi Ahai asked two scholars, Rabbi Dostai bar Rabbi Yannai and Rabbi Yosei bar Keifar, to bring back his silver vessel from Neharde'a. The people holding it handed it over, then asked the two to perform an act of acquisition making them responsible for it on the way. When they refused, the people demanded the vessel back. Rabbi Dostai agreed; Rabbi Yosei refused, so the people tormented him, and Rabbi Dostai told them, "Hit him." Back home Rabbi Yosei complained, and Rabbi Dostai explained that these frightening men would restrain or kill on command; once Rabbi Ahai learned they were close to the government and had servants at their bidding, he told Rabbi Dostai he had acted well.
why: The Gemara is asking who bears responsibility for property sent through an agent and when the sender may take it back. Just before, Rav Sheshet's agent dodged a similar acquisition; this case adds holders who demand the item back, and an agent excused because he faced danger.

people.name: Rabbi Ahai, son of Rabbi Yoshiya
people.about: Owner of a silver vessel kept in Neharde'a, who sent the two scholars to bring it to him.

people.name: Rabbi Dostai bar Rabbi Yannai
people.about: One of the two agents; he agreed to return the vessel and told the holders to hit his companion.

people.name: Rabbi Yosei bar Keifar
people.about: The other agent; he refused to give the vessel back and was tormented for it.

terms.meaning: A formal legal act that transfers ownership or responsibility. Here, performing one would have made the agents answerable for the vessel until it reached its owner.
A city in Babylonia where the vessel was being kept.
